subject: grayWolf
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: gray wolf standing alert.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module for a stylized gray wolf in an alert standing pose, Blizzard/Warcraft-inspired, using the core SDK's builder, joints, limbs, and surface tools while keeping the API usage safe and the scope manageable.

I'm working out proportions based on real gray wolf anatomy—roughly 0.8m shoulder height and 1.6m nose-to-tail length—then sketching a skeleton with a spine chain from hips to chest and limb-based legs using IK targets for the shoulders and feet.

For the legs I'm figuring out segment lengths and bend directions so joints look natural: front elbows bending backward, hind legs with hock and knee bending in opposite directions, adjusting lengths until the reach between hip/shoulder and foot positions looks anatomically right.

Now I'm planning the naming convention for limb chains (shoulder/elbow/paw per side) and setting up a reusable leg-building helper, then moving to the neck/head chain and a tail chain held low and level for an alert pose with the head raised.

I'm also defining the spine joints and chain structure, placing hips as the root joint and building the spine chain up to the chest, figuring out how to reference the chest/neck start point from the chain's joint list.

Then I'm setting up the neck chain from the chest to head base using a catmull path, and attaching the head joint to the end of that chain with a forward-upward aim direction.

Now I'm adding a jaw joint parented to the head, positioned slightly forward and down using local offsets, and planning the head geometry as a sphere-based shape.

For the skull, muzzle, and ears I'm using the part scale option on sphere and cone primitives, and sketching a tapered muzzle sweep from the head joint with a decreasing radius profile.

Still placing the ear geometry...

Now for eyes, I'm thinking of using decals on the head surface for the amber wolf eyes with dark slits, targeting the head joint's surface for positioning.

For the coat, I'm planning a Warcraft-style stylized grey wolf with slate blue shadows and a cream chest/muzzle, using cel shading to separate lit and shadow regions.

Writing coat shader logic...

Now I'm setting feet positions so paws rest flush with the ground at zero, and building the tail chain with a catmull-rom spline through four control points, naming the three resulting bone segments.

I'm giving the tail a sweep profile that tapers from thicker base to thinner tip, with a black tip coloring, posed in an alert, mostly-straight-out position. For the spine, I'm reconsidering how the hips root joint relates to the spine chain's first joint, trying to avoid a duplicate point where the chain and the hips bone would overlap.

For the limbs, I'm setting up parent relationships so shoulders attach to the chest spine joint and hips attach to the root hips joint, then building each leg as a chain of points (root, elbow/knee, foot) with corresponding segment lengths and names for each bone.

Adding paw spheres at the foot joints...

Now I'm sketching the chest as a swept barrel shape along the spine path, with radius varying by position—narrower at the hips, widest in the middle, slightly tapering toward the chest.

Still shaping the muzzle sweep...

Now adding the nose sphere positioned near the muzzle tip, a jaw joint parented to the head with its own small wedge sweep for the lower jaw, and ear shapes extruded from triangular outlines.

Placing eyes on the head's sphere surface near the front, with rim detailing for definition. For the mane, I'm considering scattering fur cards along the neck sweep using the surface scatter approach, though it feels a bit experimental.

Now I'm working out the spine fur tufts with dark grey coloring and a count around 120, plus making sure the chest cream coloring blends correctly using the fur edge normal threshold. I'm also setting the alert pose with head raised and ears forward, and finalizing the color palette with body grey, cream, and dark tones.

For eyes I'm using an amber glow effect applied to the textured eye part, and nose in dark charcoal with a possible gradient darkening the tail tip. Now I'm setting up the imports for the module, pulling in the builder helpers, fur and toon shading utilities, and SVG decal support needed to construct the creature.

Writing wolf coat material...

Writing SVG tuft texture...

Now I'm setting up the wolf's skeletal builder, starting with the hips joint and a spine chain running from the lower back up toward the shoulders using a catmull-rom curve through key points.

I'm chaining the neck next, defining a curve from the base of the neck up to the head and attaching it to the spine's second joint, working through naming conventions for each segment as I go.

Now I'm placing the head joint at the end of the neck chain with an aim point angled slightly upward to convey an alert pose, then adding a jaw joint parented to the head using local offsets for position and aim direction.

Still writing skeleton joints...

Now I'm defining the tail as a catmull-rom chain with three segments tapering in radius, giving the tip a darker color band, and then setting up a symmetric leg-building loop that computes shoulder and paw positions mirrored across the left and right sides using a limb helper with specified bone lengths and bend direction.

Still writing leg sweep and paw geometry...

Setting the bend directions so the knee angles forward and the hock angles back, matching natural hind leg posture. I'm working out unique joint names for the hind chain to avoid clashing with the front leg names.

Still writing joint hierarchy...

Still shaping the head geometry...

Adding cream cheek ruffs and ear shapes...

Positioning the ear planes so their thickness axis runs laterally across the head, giving them a flat triangular shape angled outward for an alert look. Now I'm working on placing the eye decals symmetrically on each side of the head.

Working out eye placement math...

I'm deciding to skip the brow detail and instead plan fur ruff tufts, scattering points along the neck and spine surface with a minimum distance filter based on normal direction.

For the tufts, I'm generating card-based fur geometry with size, lean, and flow parameters, tinting them with the coat color, and checking whether the grey drawing's saturation is distinct enough to register as a colored tint.

I still need to filter the fur so it stays on the back rather than the belly, limiting the ruff to the neck area, and build the body sweep from the spine chain before applying the surface. I'll also sweep the tail separately, skip detailed claws in favor of simple toe spheres, and add an extra chest/shoulder blob for heavier front-end mass.

Now I'm placing hip blobs and double-checking the final structure returns the root correctly, with all variables actually used and unused imports like noise and paint dropped. I'm also verifying the bezier signature and that foot placement sits properly on the ground plane.

I'm fine-tuning the foot and paw sphere y-coordinates and scale so the lowest points sink just slightly into the floor rather than floating, settling on a target y around 0.025 for the foot joint and 0.02 for the paw sphere with a 0.05 radius scale.

Setting front and hind paw positions and checking the tail sweep radius clears the floor, then moving on to write the final code.
